evidence: HfO2 thin films were deposited by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using Hf[(C2H5)(CH3)N]4 and H2O2 at a temperature range of 175–325 ◦C. Ar was used as a purging and carrier gas. Tetrakis-ethylmethylaminohafnium (Hf[(C2H5)(CH3)N]4, TEMAHf) was used as a Hf source. The Hf precursor, which was held in a bubbler at 50 ◦C, was delivered into the reactor using an Ar gas flow rate of 400 sccm, and 50 wt% H2O2 was used as an oxygen source.
